full.description: This is a low-power photomicrograph of thyroid tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The histological section demonstrates extensive lymphocytic infiltration, lymphoid follicle formation with germinal centers, and Hurthle cell metaplasia. These prominent features are characteristic of Hashimoto's thyroiditis, an autoimmune thyroid disease.

random.description: This is a low-power photomicrograph of thyroid tissue showing a nodular or multinodular architecture. The section demonstrates multiple hyperplastic thyroid follicles filled with colloid, surrounded by fibrous septa and lymphocytic infiltration. The histologic features are consistent with a multinodular goiter or adenomatous goiter.
captions: Necrotizing squamous metaplasia of prostate, mimicking SCC. This transurethral resection of the prostate after ablative therapy shows necrotizing squamous metaplasia within the hyperplastic prostate glands mimicking SCC. At low power, lobulated appearance of the lesion (a) and, at high power (b), lack of definitive infiltrative features suggest the diagnosis of squamous metaplasia.

. Ependymoma. There is a fibrillary background and a tendency for the cells to line up around vessels (arrow), with the ependymal cell processes extending to the vessel and the nuclei around the perimeter. This is actually an example of a pseudorosette; true rosettes have a lumen, not a vessel, at the center.
